verdict.rationale: Sentry's source is publicly readable: there is a getsentry/sentry GitHub repo, all of Sentry can be self-hosted for free, and users report reading the code to build advanced integrations. However, community evidence says Sentry moved to the BSL, and one user now calls it closed-source, so whether the license counts as 'open' is uncertain. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of the license terms, and evidence that the current license is an OSI-approved open-source license rather than source-available BSL.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: How you can run all of Sentry on your own server, without paying anything.
the fully open source code helped a ton with advanced integrations, since they could see exactly what happens instead of relying only on the docs
